plans.rationale: Initial round of evidence gathering to establish the exact symptom onset for payments-api and identify any concurrent changes or upstream/downstream dependency issues.

tasks.goal: Check metrics and logs for payments-api and its immediate dependencies to establish exact symptom onset, error rates, and check the frequency and timing of TLS deprecation warnings.
Identify all recent deploys, configuration changes, infrastructure modifications, and feature flags across all services, and inspect the dependency map around payments-api.

r1-observability-1.summary: Observability metrics show that payments-api p99 latency spiked significantly from ~382ms to over 3.2s starting at 2026-10-11T13:20:00+00:00, with error rates increasing from ~0.3% to ~1.2%. ledger-service p99 latency also spiked from ~120ms to over 3.1s starting at 2026-10-11T13:19:00+00:00. TLS deprecation warnings in payments-api are constant throughout the window (from 12:00 onwards) and therefore unrelated to the onset of the latency anomaly.

findings.statement: payments-api p99 latency increased from baseline ~382.67ms to 3239.85ms at 2026-10-11T13:20:00+00:00, peaking at 3521.46ms at 13:27.
payments-api error rate increased from ~0.3% to ~1.2% starting around 2026-10-11T13:25:00+00:00.
ledger-service p99 latency increased from baseline ~120.79ms to 3196.98ms starting at 2026-10-11T13:19:00+00:00, peaking at 3364.94ms at 13:23:00+00:00.
TLS deprecation warnings in payments-api logs occurred continuously from 12:00:00+00:00 onwards (total 2289 occurrences), preceding the latency spike by over an hour.
fraud-service and upi-gateway did not show anomalous latency or error rate spikes during the incident window.

open_questions: What caused ledger-service latency to spike at 13:19:00+00:00?

r1-dependency-2.summary: Completed dependency mapping and 7-day change audit for payments-api and related services. payments-api depends synchronously on ledger-service, upi-gateway, fraud-service, and redis-cache, and is called by mobile-bff. A significant feature flag rollout on ledger-service (ledger.reconciliation_v2 10% to 100%) occurred at 13:18 UTC, shortly before the incident onset (~13:20 UTC).

findings.statement: payments-api depends synchronously on mobile-bff (upstream caller), ledger-service, upi-gateway, fraud-service, and redis-cache, and asynchronously on event-bus.
upi-gateway depends synchronously on npci-switch and partner-bank-api.
ledger-service had a feature flag rollout chg-9802 (ledger.reconciliation_v2 from 10% to 100%) at 2026-10-11T13:18:00+00:00, which precedes the reported latency symptom onset at ~13:20 UTC.
redis-session and user-db had routine releases and redis-session had a config rotation earlier on 2026-10-11.

open_questions: Did the full rollout of ledger.reconciliation_v2 in ledger-service cause increased latency or load on ledger-db or payments-api?
Are external dependencies like npci-switch or partner-bank-api contributing to transaction slowdowns through upi-gateway?

hypotheses.title: Ledger reconciliation feature flag rollout causes latency spike
hypotheses.mechanism: The rollout of the ledger.reconciliation_v2 feature flag from 10% to 100% on ledger-service introduced blocking or inefficient reconciliation processing, causing ledger-service p99 latency to spike at 13:19 UTC, which propagated to synchronous dependent payments-api at 13:20 UTC.

supporting.note: Feature flag change at 13:18 UTC immediately precedes the ledger-service latency spike at 13:19 UTC.
Shows ledger-service p99 latency spiking sharply upward starting at 13:19.
Shows payments-api p99 latency spiking starting at 13:20.
Confirms synchronous dependency from payments-api to ledger-service.

contradicting.note: Ledger-service CPU percentage showed no notable anomaly during the incident window.
Ledger-service error rate remained stable without an anomaly during the window.

assumptions: The new reconciliation logic under ledger.reconciliation_v2 causes thread waiting or I/O waits rather than high CPU usage.

hypotheses.title: Ledger database degradation causes cascading latency
hypotheses.mechanism: Underlying performance bottlenecks or lock issues in ledger-db caused slow queries for ledger-service starting earlier at 12:23 UTC, escalating into a severe slowdown at 13:19 UTC that cascaded to payments-api.

supporting.note: Ledger-service logged warnings about retrying calls to ledger-db starting at 12:23 UTC.
Confirms ledger-service latency spike starting at 13:19 UTC.
Confirms payments-api latency spike starting at 13:20 UTC.

contradicting.note: Feature flag change at 13:18 UTC provides a much tighter temporal correlation to the sharp onset at 13:19 than database warnings occurring hours prior.

assumptions: The earlier db warnings represented an incipient database degradation that independently worsened at 13:19 UTC.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: We establish symptom onset at 13:19 UTC for ledger-service and 13:20 UTC for payments-api. H1 is the primary hypothesis because the feature flag rollout chg-9802 at 13:18 UTC precisely precedes the onset. H2 attributes the issue to underlying ledger-db degradation starting from earlier log warnings, but it lacks the tight temporal correlation of the feature flag change.

adjustments.reason: The feature flag rollout chg-9802 on ledger-service at 13:18 UTC directly precedes the sharp p99 latency spike starting at 13:19 UTC on ledger-service and propagating to payments-api at 13:20 UTC. All automatic checks pass cleanly.
Database warnings occurred hours prior and do not align with the sudden onset at 13:19 UTC.
